_about: The guest register, in alphabetical order of guest name. Supplied by the host on 24 November 2026 as three images and transcribed word for word, apart from the host's own name corrections (see docs/CHARACTERS.md). 'occupation' is the original character heading. 'publicRole' is what the site shows openly: where the original heading gives away something the Public Story does not, it is shortened or left empty until the host decides. 'privateBackstory' is never written into the page as readable text: it is obscured at build time and only shown after the guest confirms the dossier is theirs. That is a courtesy barrier, not security.

guests.publicStory: Howdy, folks. Bobby ‘The Bookie’ Thompson here. I spend my evenings managing the gambling tables and keeping track of the numbers. It’s a job that requires patience, attention, and a good memory. After all, people reveal a lot about themselves when money is involved.
guests.privateBackstory: You ran Johnny’s gambling operations under the protection of his name, but lately, Johnny was more risk than reward. His debt to dangerous people threatened to collapse everything you built. And watching him get closer to Rosie O’Hara only made it worse. You’ve had feelings for Rosie for years, and Johnny’s presence always stood in your way. When you overheard Johnny talking about settling a dangerous debt, you knew someone would make a move on him, and you didn’t stop it. Maybe you didn’t kill him, but you didn’t protect him either. Now, your note linking you to Johnny the night he died is raising suspicion. You need to shift attention elsewhere and protect both your operation and your feelings for Rosie.

guests.publicStory: Greetings. Name’s Rocco Barone. I worked closely with Johnny for years as his right hand man and helped look after the day-to-day operations of The Velvet Cellar. He built this place and I made sure no one messed with it, or him. Loyalty means a great deal to me, and I’ve always taken pride in protecting the people and places that matter.
guests.privateBackstory: You were Johnny’s bodyguard: fiercely loyal, the muscle behind the man. To you, Johnny wasn’t just a boss; he was family. But near the end, things got messy. He was gambling with dangerous people and wouldn’t listen to reason, no matter how hard you tried to protect him from himself. You found a threatening letter in his office a few days before his death; someone in the syndicate wanted him gone. You kept it quiet, hoping it would help you track the traitor. Now Johnny’s dead, and you’re torn: part of you saw it coming, but most of you still wants revenge. You’re determined to protect what Johnny built, sniff out whoever betrayed him, and keep snakes like Vincent Valenti from seizing control.

guests.publicStory: Detective Cleo Adams at your service. I’ve spent years investigating crimes, interviewing witnesses, and following the facts wherever they lead. I pay attention to details, ask a lot of questions, and don’t draw conclusions until I have the evidence to support them.
guests.privateBackstory: You were brought into the investigation due to suspicions about Johnny’s mob connections, but this case is personal. Your brother was a victim of mob violence, and it’s fueled your relentless drive to take down anyone connected to organized crime. Johnny’s murder offers a chance to expose the bigger criminal network, and your instincts tell you that something is off with the people around him. Sam Spade, in particular, raises suspicions; his behavior seems too eager to close the case, and you feel he’s hiding something. As you dig deeper, you uncover an incriminating document linking Vincent Valenti to shady financial dealings with Johnny. You know this document could be the key to unraveling the larger syndicate behind Johnny’s death, but revealing it might put you in danger. You must decide who you can trust while continuing your investigation, determined to bring justice for your brother and expose the criminal empire that took his life.

guests.publicStory: Evening! Margaret ‘Maggie’ Sinclair here. Johnny brought me into The Velvet Cellar back when it was just a dream with a dirty floor. I’ve been here ever since, helping build this place into what it is today. He’s gone now, and I’ll be damned if I let everything we built fall into the wrong hands.
guests.privateBackstory: You were Johnny’s secret partner, an investor, a strategist, and the silent force behind The Velvet Cellar’s rise. You reaped the profits while Johnny played the flashy frontman. But as his ego grew, so did your problems. Johnny got sloppy. He bragged too loudly, risked too much, and worst of all, hinted at revealing your role when tensions with Vincent flared. When Johnny died, you lost your buffer. Now you’re exposed, vulnerable, and forced to play the game yourself. Maybe you had a hand in his demise. Maybe you didn’t. Either way, you’re going to make damn sure the power he left behind ends up in the right hands: yours.

guests.publicStory: What’s the haps? I’m Daisy, but you can call me ‘Doll.’ I sell flowers, sometimes deliver a message or two. The folks here are real nice, at least most of the time. I help out however I can, just like Papa says.
guests.privateBackstory: You sell flowers at The Velvet Cellar, often weaving through the crowd unnoticed as you work. People have a tendency to overlook you, which has allowed you to overhear more than your fair share of secrets. You sometimes even passed along messages, unknowingly becoming part of Johnny’s network. Since Johnny’s death, you’re trying your best to stay out of trouble, but you fear you know too much. Keeping your family safe is your top priority, but it’s hard to forget the things you’ve heard.

guests.publicStory: Well, this is a full house. They call me Duke ‘Dapper’ Monroe. I’m a regular at the card tables and enjoy a good game almost as much as good company. I’ve spent years studying people, and I’ve found they’re often easier to read than they think.
guests.privateBackstory: You’re a professional gambler: charming, slick, and sharp as a fresh deck. Johnny ran a crooked but reliable game, and The Velvet Cellar was your home turf. You weren’t involved in the mob side of things, but you weren’t blind, either. The night before Johnny died, you played cards with him. He was tense, distracted. Said something about a debt gone wrong and a meeting with someone “he couldn’t afford to lose to.” You figured he was bluffing… until he wound up dead. Now rumors are swirling. You overheard Bobby trying to play down a note with his initials (something about a late night meeting with Johnny). That note reeks of setup, or worse. Bobby’s hiding something. You don’t know if he killed Johnny, but you’re betting he knows who did, and you’re not letting him off the hook.

guests.publicStory: Ladies and gents, Ruby ‘Red’ O’Connell here at your service, but just call me Ruby. I run the cigarette and candy stand here at The Velvet Cellar. I enjoy getting to know the regulars and making sure guests have what they need. Johnny always believed good service kept people coming back, so I have done my best to help with that.
guests.privateBackstory: You started working at The Velvet Cellar to earn extra cash, but soon realized your position as a cigarette girl gave you access to secrets. The night Johnny died, you were near Sam, and your presence serves as his alibi, and his yours. But now, you’re starting to wonder if you might have played a bigger role than you remember. Could you have done something in a moment of confusion? Your knowledge of the people and conversations around Johnny makes you a potential target or ally, but you’re unsure if sharing what you know will help or hurt you. For now, you’re trying to keep a low profile and protect your secrets, all while questioning what role you really played in Johnny’s death.

guests.occupation: Investigative Journalist with Ties to Mob Investigations
guests.publicStory: Hello, hello, what a crowd! I’m Virginia ‘Jinx’ Jameson, and it’s a pleasure to meet all of you tonight. If you know me, you know I’m always on the hunt for the juiciest secrets, as a reporter for the local newspaper. My job is to ask questions, gather facts, and keep up with what’s happening around town.
guests.privateBackstory: You’re an ambitious journalist who’s spent years digging into corruption, coverups, and the people behind them. The Velvet Cellar was just another lead, until Johnny turned up dead. Now? It’s a full blown expose waiting to happen. Your secret source, Dominic Russo, has been feeding you intel from inside Vincent Valenti’s criminal network. But playing both sides is dangerous because if anyone finds out you’re getting help, you won’t be walking out of here with your story, or your life. Still, you know too much to back down now. Johnny’s death is only the beginning. There’s power swirling in this room, from mobsters, to crooked politicians, to insiders, and your job is to get the story straight without ending up in tomorrow’s headline yourself. You’ve kept detailed notes in your reporter’s journal while observing patrons in The Velvet Cellar. One odd thing stands out: Johnny referred to someone by the initials “FR” during a tense conversation in the back room a few nights before his death. You didn’t know what it meant at the time, but it felt important. You logged it anyway. Now, with whispers flying and tensions rising, you might have the missing piece someone else is desperate to find.

guests.publicStory: I’m Reggie Callahan, but most folks just call me Rook. I used to throw punches for a living, now I keep The Velvet Cellar safe. Johnny gave me a second shot when I had nothin’ left but busted knuckles. He kept this place together… and I’m not about to let someone tear it apart.
guests.privateBackstory: You were a rising boxing star once, but one bad fight and a shattered shoulder ended all that. Johnny gave you a job, a suit, and a reason to stay sober. Since then, you’ve kept trouble off the floor and loyalty in your bones. But the night Johnny died, something changed. You were outside his office during a heated argument: raised voices, threats. You didn’t see who went in, but you caught a woman’s voice: cold, polished, commanding. It wasn’t Ruby, and it sure wasn’t Clara. The more you’ve thought about it, the more you’re sure it was Lena Luciano. She’s been showing up more often since Johnny’s death; she’s making suggestions, smiling too much, asking too many questions. You don’t trust her. You’re not one for politics, but you know a power play when you see one.

guests.publicStory: Hello, darlings. I’m Gloria ‘Goldie’ Delaney, one of the featured singers here at The Velvet Cellar. I spend my evenings under the spotlight, entertaining the crowd, meeting interesting people, and enjoying good conversation. I’ve heard more than my fair share around this club, but these lips? [Smile slowly and sultrily] They stay sealed unless I’ve got a very good reason to open them [blow a kiss to the crowd].
guests.privateBackstory: Once Johnny’s shining star, you were more than just his headliner; you were his secret partner in a smuggling ring that helped keep The Velvet Cellar afloat. You never signed anything, never left a trail, but Angelo found out anyway. Now he’s blackmailing you, threatening to ruin you if you don’t play nice. Johnny, ever the dreamer, wanted to go legit. That meant shutting down the smuggling, and exposing the people who helped him run it. You tried to convince him to keep it quiet, but he wouldn’t listen. Then, just like that, he was dead. Did someone silence him for you? Or did fate just hand you a way out? Either way, Johnny’s death didn’t free you; it pushed you straight under Angelo’s boot. You’re walking a tightrope, using every ounce of charm and cunning you have to survive. One wrong step, and your whole act falls apart.

guests.publicStory: Well, well, well, Angelo Rossi at your service. I’m an attorney by trade and have spent years representing some of the city’s most influential figures. A sharp mind, careful preparation, and strong relationships have served me well. When challenges arise, people know they can count on me to handle them.
guests.privateBackstory: You were Johnny’s legal fixer, until he became a threat. His carelessness and cocky attitude were going to take everyone down, and you couldn’t let that happen. You didn’t kill him yourself, but you orchestrated his downfall by leaking just enough to get the right people watching. You’ve since wiped your fingerprints clean from Johnny’s records and tampered with his ledger to erase any ties between his illegal dealings and your firm. Now, you’re manipulating Gloria to keep her quiet, blackmailing her with a secret from her past. Meanwhile, you’ve caught wind that Brody might’ve snapped a damning photo of you near Johnny’s office. If that image surfaces, your entire career, and freedom, could vanish.

guests.occupation: Former Gang Member Turned Social Reformer
guests.publicRole: Former Gang Member Turned Social Reformer
guests.publicStory: Evening! How’s the night treating you? I’m Ruth ‘Redemption’ Reynolds. Used to run with the wrong crowd, but I’ve made peace with my past… mostly. People can change if they’re willing to put in the work, so I’ve spent the last few years doing exactly that. Johnny’s death has stirred things up again, and here I am back in the place I swore I left behind.
guests.privateBackstory: You used to run bootlegging routes for Johnny: fast, fearless, and loyal. Then came a prison stint and a reckoning. You got out, rebuilt yourself, and now help others escape the cycle of crime. But walking the straight path is harder when the streets keep calling. When you heard about Johnny’s murder, something pulled you back. You started digging, and what you found chilled you: a hidden ledger listing every crooked deal and dirty name Johnny touched. Vincent, sure. But also Lena Luciano, who’s built her reputation on respectability. She was deeper in it than anyone thought. You haven’t shared this ledger yet. It could collapse Lena’s empire, spark a war… or buy you favors. You’re not sure if you’re the crusader or the threat. But you know one thing: if Lena’s playing both sides, someone needs to stop her.

guests.publicStory: How do, buckaroo? Dexter Cooper’s the name. I enjoy books, good conversation, and figuring things out. People sometimes underestimate me, but I have a habit of noticing details that others miss.
guests.privateBackstory: You’re a deep cover federal agent embedded in The Velvet Cellar, sent to investigate Johnny McGraw’s bootlegging ring and its ties to organized crime. You’ve spent months gaining trust, documenting meetings, and using coded jazz setlists to record criminal activity without blowing your cover. Lately, things spiraled. Johnny got sloppy: making risky deals, drawing attention, and dragging innocents into his mess. You feared he’d collapse the whole operation before you could finish the job. When he arranged a late night meeting with someone using the alias “FR,” you logged the details in your cipher: time, place, behavior. Then Johnny turned up dead. Now that encrypted note is missing. You don’t know who picked it up, but only that if it’s decoded and misinterpreted, it could either expose a key suspect… or falsely implicate someone you swore to protect. Every conversation feels like a landmine. And someone (maybe Freddy, maybe worse) is holding a match. You’re stuck between your mission and the truth, unsure who to trust, and running out of time.

guests.publicStory: Howdy, folks! Clara ‘Hope’ Bennett here. I’ve seen how Prohibition has made the poor desperate and the rich richer. I’m here tonight to build support for social reform and advocate for working families. But lately, I’ve started noticing things at The Velvet Cellar that don’t sit right with me. I intend to find out what’s really going on.
guests.privateBackstory: You are a dedicated social worker who believed in Johnny’s charitable contributions, until you discovered his misuse of those funds. The realization cut deeply, as Johnny had deceived you and the very people you were trying to protect. You confronted him in anger, tearing your sleeve during a heated exchange in his office. As you stormed out, you noticed someone lingering nearby, though you couldn’t see who it was. Driven by a sense of betrayal and a need to right the wrongs Johnny caused, you’re now determined to seek justice, and not just for yourself, but for all the vulnerable people Johnny exploited. Your name must be cleared, and you’re resolved to uncover the truth of what really happened that night, even if it means confronting the painful reality of both what Johnny became and what you’ve done.

guests.publicStory: Hey there, darlings! Josie Bennett here: the queen of the dance floor and sparkle of The Velvet Cellar. I spend most of my evenings here enjoying the music, dancing with friends, and meeting new people. I love a lively crowd and never miss an opportunity to have a good time.
guests.privateBackstory: Everyone sees you as the heart of the party, but what they don’t see is how carefully you work to keep that image untouchable. Lately, Johnny had been unraveling. His reckless decisions were putting everything at risk: the fun, the freedom, the life you built under these speakeasy lights. You heard whispers of shady deals and saw shadows where there used to be shine. And then, he ended up dead. Now you’re stuck pretending everything’s fine, even as you quietly piece things together. You overheard a tense exchange the night of the murder: Johnny and someone unfamiliar, voices low but charged. You didn’t catch the details, but you felt the danger. You’ve kept your mouth shut, but for how long? Part of you wonders… maybe someone had to do it. Johnny’s spiral could’ve taken everyone down. Still, the thought scares you. And now you’re dancing a fine line between staying safe and staying curious.

guests.publicStory: Hi, Misters and Missus. Name’s Timmy ‘Junior’ Johnson, but most folks just call me Junior. I shine shoes, run errands, and get things done for a few coins. I know this place better than most of the fellas inside. Don’t let my age fool ya because I see more than I let on.
guests.privateBackstory: You’ve spent most of your life making yourself useful to survive: shining shoes, carrying notes, staying quiet. Johnny kept you around the club, and for a while, that meant safety. But lately? Everyone’s been tense. The night Johnny died, you saw too much and now you don’t know who to trust. You spotted Angelo slipping into Johnny’s office earlier that evening, right before the shouting started. Then came the note he made you deliver, all secretive and rushed. Later, you caught Vincent whispering with someone in the shadows, and when the shouting started again, you kept your head down, pretending not to hear. But you heard everything. Johnny had dirt on everyone. He was threatening to blow it all open, including what he knew about you. You hated that. You needed him gone, but you didn’t dare act. Now he’s dead, and you’re trapped between guilt, fear, and survival. If the wrong person finds out what you know… you’re toast. But if you play this right? You might finally have a way out.

guests.publicStory: Good evening all. I am Dr. Hughes, the county medical examiner. My job is to examine the evidence, document the facts, and determine what happened. I trust careful observation more than assumptions, and I take my work very seriously.
guests.privateBackstory: As the medical examiner, you initially trusted Detective Sam Spade, but his eagerness to close Johnny’s case raised red flags. The toxicology report revealed poison, and your suspicion grew: Johnny was silenced. But the deeper you dig, the more terrifying the truth becomes. You’ve spent years altering reports and covering for shady figures in exchange for funding your personal research (some of them connected to Johnny). Now you’re wondering if your silence, your compromises, even your paperwork… helped kill him. Worse, you suspect Sam might know. You’re trying to expose the truth, but every new clue risks uncovering your own role. If it all comes out, you could go down with the killer.

guests.publicStory: Evenin’ all, name’s Detective Samuel Spade. I am the detective folks call when things go south. I’ve spent years investigating crimes and sorting through conflicting stories to find the truth. Johnny was a friend, and I intend to learn what happened. If you’re looking for me, I’ll probably be near the bar with a glass of whiskey and a few questions.
guests.privateBackstory: You were Johnny’s private detective and head of security: trusted with his secrets, until he started digging into yours. He uncovered evidence of your bribes and backroom deals, and you knew it was only a matter of time before he used it to ruin you. The night he died, you argued loudly. You mixed whiskey with sleeping pills, so you remember shouting, threats, but the rest is blacked out. You woke up groggy, with hours unaccounted for. Ruby said she saw you stumbling near the back exit around the time Johnny died, but you don’t remember. Then you found Clara’s torn dress in Johnny’s office. Willy’s obsession with the toxicology report makes you uneasy, especially since you can’t remember what you did. He keeps hinting at poison, and if he has proof, it could bury you, whether you’re guilty or not. Worse, if he reveals what he knows about your past… you won’t just lose your job; you’ll lose everything. What if your blackout wasn’t just meds and booze? What if you did something you can’t remember? You want the truth. But deep down, you’re terrified of what it might be.

guests.publicStory: How do you do? I’m Freddy Brooks, the local paperboy. I spend my days delivering newspapers and keeping up with what’s happening around town. People don’t pay much attention to a paperboy, but you’d be surprised what you can learn when you’re always around. You want the word on the street? I got it.
guests.privateBackstory: You’ve made yourself a fixture at The Velvet Cellar: dropping off papers, running errands, delivering messages. Johnny liked you, paid you fair, and treated you decently. That meant something. His death has thrown the whole place into chaos, and now you’re trying to figure out who’s taking over… and whether they’ll be as kind. Recently, you found a torn note near Johnny’s office. It was jumbled with strange letters, music titles, and numbers. You hid it, assuming it was something shady Johnny left behind. The night before Johnny was found dead, you also saw Vincent slip out of the Cellar muttering something about “taking care of things.” It scared you. Now, you’re holding onto these secrets. Maybe they’ll protect you… or maybe they’ll put you in more danger.

guests.publicStory: Well, hello there, darlings! I’m Lena Luciano. I’ve spent years building relationships with the city’s business and political leaders, and I take pride in knowing how things get done. I enjoy being involved in important decisions, and I rarely miss an opportunity to advance my interests.
guests.privateBackstory: You’re a rising star in city politics, but your clean image is nothing but smoke and mirrors. Behind closed doors, you were taking bribes from Johnny McGraw to keep The Velvet Cellar safe from law enforcement. His bootlegging operation helped bankroll your campaign (until his unpredictability became a liability). You warned him to stay quiet, stay smart, and stay in line. He didn’t listen. Now Johnny’s dead, and every whispered deal and shady payout threatens to unravel. Whether or not you were behind his death, you know one thing: your empire can’t fall with him. You need to shift the blame, secure new alliances, and play everyone just right… before the truth plays you.

guests.publicStory: I don’t make a habit of introducing myself to strangers, but here we are. Name’s Dominic ‘Dom’ Russo. I’m the guy who gets things where they need to be: quietly, no fuss. I handle deliveries and transportation for a variety of clients around town. My work requires discretion, reliability, and keeping to myself, which suits me just fine.
guests.privateBackstory: You’ve been the quiet backbone of Vincent’s empire for years, keeping shipments moving, questions silenced, and operations smooth. But you’re tired. Tired of the pressure, the violence, and the constant risk. That’s why you’ve been slipping information to Jinx: an undercover journalist who promises a clean slate if you help her bring down the right people. The plan was simple: leak just enough dirt to get out before anyone noticed. But then Johnny started spiraling. Debts, threats, big talk. He was drawing heat to everyone, including you. He didn’t know about your connection to Jinx, but he was getting too close. Whether you wanted it or not, Johnny’s death cleared a dangerous obstacle. Still, if anyone finds out what you’ve been up to, you’re next on the list. Now you’re walking a tightrope: feeding Jinx, dodging Vincent, and keeping suspicions off your back. You’ll do what it takes to disappear before the whole thing burns down, but just not before tying up a few loose ends.

guests.publicStory: Folks, I’m Vincent Valenti. I run a successful business operation in this city and have spent years building valuable connections. Johnny and I worked together on more than one venture, and I have a strong interest in seeing our affairs remain in capable hands.
guests.privateBackstory: You are the leader of the local syndicate, and your business relationship with Johnny was built on mutual benefit. Lately, Johnny’s erratic behavior threatened everything you had built. When he discovered your profit skimming from The Velvet Cellar, it became a direct threat to your operations. You warned him to get his act together, but Johnny’s loose lips and reckless attitude put your empire at risk. The night before he died, your argument with him escalated, but you couldn’t afford for Johnny to continue jeopardizing everything. Now, with him out of the way, you see an opportunity to consolidate power and eliminate a dangerous liability. You’ve put your trusted lieutenants, Angelo, Marco, Mina, Jinx, and Dom, to work, ensuring no one links you to Johnny’s demise. You’ve forged a financial document to make it seem Johnny owed you money, hoping to cover your tracks. Your goal is to secure your empire, protect your illicit dealings, and remove any threat to your control without drawing suspicion.

guests.publicStory: Heya, toots! I’m Rosie O’Hara, one of the featured performers here at The Velvet Cellar. I’ve been entertaining guests for years and wouldn’t trade the spotlight for anything. If you’ve come looking for a good time tonight, you’ve come to the right place.
guests.privateBackstory: As the star performer at The Velvet Cellar, you were secretly involved with Johnny. It wasn’t all love songs and moonlight, though; his reckless behavior had started putting everything you built at risk. You overheard him in a heated argument shortly before he died, but the shadows were thick, and you couldn’t make out who it was. The voice… maybe Bobby? Maybe Sam? You weren’t sure, but it shook you. Bobby Thompson is the one person you trust most here, or used to. Lately, he’s been distant, twitchy. You want to believe in him, but doubt has crept in. Worse still, your secret with Johnny could ruin your life if it comes out. You’re torn between loyalty, grief, and fear. You’re not here to play detective, but someone has to get to the truth before fingers start pointing at you… or at Bobby.

guests.publicStory: Well, what have we here? A group of lively souls gathered at the finest spot in town! Cheers to new beginnings! I’m Gigi Moreau. I’m one of the performers here at The Velvet Cellar, and there’s nothing I enjoy more than entertaining a crowd. A good song, a lively audience, and a night spent on stage suit me just fine.
guests.privateBackstory: You’re more than just The Velvet Cellar’s star singer; you’re also an informant with an ear for secrets and a knack for slipping between circles unnoticed. Johnny knew how to play the game, and you liked the way he protected your space here. But lately, things had felt… off. You overheard Sam called by the strange alias “FR” more than once (once by Johnny himself when he didn’t think anyone was listening). You’ve been keeping tabs ever since. With Johnny gone, the game just changed, and if you play your cards right, you’ll be the one holding the mic and the secrets when the dust settles.

guests.publicStory: Hiya everyone! I see we’ve got a room full of good company tonight. Ambrose ‘Brody’ Sawyer here. I’m a photographer, which means I’m usually the fellow behind the camera at parties, events, and celebrations. I enjoy meeting people, capturing memorable moments, and keeping an eye out for interesting stories.
guests.privateBackstory: You’re The Velvet Cellar’s photographer, capturing the allure of the speakeasy life for Johnny’s promotions. Before Johnny’s death, you accidentally photographed him arguing with an unknown figure, which may be a crucial clue. Though you’ve always been in Johnny’s shadow, watching his success overshadow yours, you never imagined it would lead to something like this. Since then, you’ve allied with Clara Bennett, whose drive for justice mirrors your own. Growing up in a tough neighborhood, you know the harm corruption brings, and Johnny’s death feels like part of something bigger, something that’s been brewing beneath the surface for a long time. Together with Clara, you’re trying to piece together the clues to uncover the truth and protect those at risk, even if it means confronting your own feelings of resentment toward Johnny’s rise to fame.

guests.publicStory: Welcome to The Velvet Cellar! Well, well, look at all these fine people gathered in one place. Pleasure to meet you folks! I’m Violet ‘Vivi’ St. James, here to make sure your night’s one to remember. Johnny knew how to treat guests, and I intend to keep up the tradition. Grab a drink, relax, and let the worries of the world melt away.
guests.privateBackstory: You started as a coat check girl and worked your way up the ladder, winning hearts with charm, wit, and intuition. Johnny trusted you. You knew everyone: who drank what, who danced with whom, who whispered when the music was loud. You were his eyes and ears on the floor, and when you caught wind of a raid last spring, it was your warning that saved his neck. But now Johnny’s gone, and with him, the protection your loyalty earned. The Velvet Cellar is on the brink of a power shift. Vincent’s circling, Maggie’s scheming, and Lena’s playing politics. You don’t want to pick a side, but staying neutral in a room full of secrets might make you a target. You’ve got one ace left: a discreet guest list from the past year, filled with names powerful enough to make or break reputations. You’re not sure when you’ll need it… but you know someone else might kill for it.

guests.publicStory: It seems like you’ve found your way in. Enjoy the night, but just don’t cross the wrong people. Name’s Marco ‘The Muscle’ DeLuca. I watch Vincent’s back and have for quite some time. I’m dependable, loyal, and not easily intimidated. You mess with him, you deal with me.
guests.privateBackstory: You’ve been Vincent Valenti’s right hand since you were old enough to throw a punch. He’s the boss, the brains, but you’re the muscle. When someone becomes a problem, you fix it. And Johnny? He was a big problem. His gambling debts, sloppy alliances, and loose lips were putting the whole operation at risk. Vincent might’ve been patient, but you weren’t. You knew Johnny’s recklessness was a threat. You also knew Vincent was getting tired of the mess. Whether you were following orders or just reading between the lines, you helped make sure Johnny wouldn’t get the chance to ruin things for everyone. Now? Everyone’s poking around, and you’ve got to play it cool. You’ll protect Vincent’s empire at all costs (even if that means handling a few loose ends yourself). You’re not afraid to get your hands dirty. You’re afraid of failing the one man who gave you everything.
